acceptance: Reproduce exited guest TID host-proc fallback deterministically with an owned live native thread; preserve the original ENOENT assertions.
Remember precisely issued guest TIDs after exit/exec without claiming sparse gaps or unrelated foreign paths; reset forked-child ownership and preserve known child PID reuse.
Keep normal sequential-ID metadata compact; test merging, splitting, extreme boundaries and sparse clone3 identities.
Compile shared behavior on Windows/macOS/Linux and execute native Linux collision checks; exact red commits, RAX two-URL and paired Assist two-remote publication.

assumptions.assumption: A missing proc entry for a retired guest thread must not resolve to an unrelated host thread with the same numeric ID.
assumptions.basis: Existing procfs lifetime test, failing Linux CI and resolver fallback trace.
assumptions.stress-test: Live host thread with same TID, bare directory/status/fd/task aliases
assumptions.falsification-probe: The guest opens the host-backed path after its matching guest thread exits

assumptions.assumption: Exact assigned-ID history must survive exec, reset in a forked child and yield to an explicitly reused owned child PID.
assumptions.basis: Current PID/TID allocation, clone3 sparse IDs and fork/exec lifecycle.
assumptions.stress-test: Sparse chosen IDs, reuse, fork reset, nonleader exec
assumptions.falsification-probe: Unissued IDs are claimed, old parent IDs remain owned by a new child, or a current child PID is hidden

planned-owned: new portable procfs lifetime tests and tests/mod.rs registration

bounded-findings.finding: Existing next_tid overflow/PID-domain behavior and potential cross-process ID collisions need separate review; do not broaden the allocation policy incidentally.
